bibliography.checked_against: the cover and abstract (PDF pp. 1–3) and the library record
bibliography.note: Fago, Don. 1977. Northern pike production in managed spawning and rearing marshes. Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources Technical Bulletin No. 96, Madison. Printed page = PDF page − 3 in the body (Table 2 on printed p. 9 = PDF p. 12).

claims.claim: northern pike egg-to-fingerling survival in Wisconsin managed marshes 0.15–2.69 % (mean 1.09 %)
claims.quote: from 0.15 to 2.69 percent with an average of 1.09 percent
claims.conditions: two managed marshes stocked each spring with adult pike: Pleasant Lake Marsh (1.5 ha, 1969–73) and Pabst Marsh (7.5 ha, 1971–72), seven marsh-years; survival = fingerlings counted at draining (25 May–13 June) ÷ eggs deposited, the eggs estimated from a fecundity–length regression × females stocked (Fago warns the egg estimates' confidence limits 'can be significant'); fingerlings 38–173 mm (mean 88.9 mm)

claims.claim: egg to 38–173-mm fingerling (~55 d): instantaneous daily mortality ~0.07–0.12 (project estimate)
claims.source_value: fingerlings 38–173 mm at draining (confirmed); the source gives no egg-to-draining interval: stocking 16 Mar–5 Apr (Table 1) to draining 25 May–13 Jun (Table 2) spans 50–78 d; year-matched Z counted from stocking = 0.072 (1972: 2.69 %, ~50 d) to 0.098 (1970: 0.15 %, ~66 d)
claims.location: Abstract (PDF p. 3); Table 1, p. 8 (PDF p. 11); Table 2, p. 9 (PDF p. 12)
claims.quote: a length range from 1.5 to 6.8 inches (38 to 173 mm)
claims.conditions: managed marshes filled at the end of March and held 'approximately nine' weeks until draining; spawning date after stocking not given
claims.note: Working: −ln(0.0015)/55 = 0.118 and −ln(0.0269)/55 = 0.066, so the paper's range follows from an assumed 55 d. With each year's own stocking-to-draining interval: 1970 (stocked 3 Apr, drained 8–11 Jun, 66–69 d) −ln(0.0015)/66 = 0.098; 1972 (stocked 5 Apr, drained 25–26 May, 50–51 d) −ln(0.0269)/50 = 0.072. If spawning lagged stocking by about a week the rates rise to ~0.08–0.11, so '~0.07–0.12' is a fair envelope, but the interval column should read 'egg to fingerling at draining (stocking to draining 50–78 d)' rather than '~55 d'.

notes: Other useful values: production 324–3,243 fingerlings/acre (131–1,312/ha) at Pleasant Lake and 681–1,052/acre at Pabst; 2.5–18.3 kg/ha of fingerlings; Fago names water temperature and dissolved oxygen during draining, cannibalism in the fingerling stage and zooplankton composition in the fry stage as the most important influences (abstract). Table 3 (PDF p. 13) compiles egg-to-fingerling survival from managed marshes in six states (not read cell by cell here; the text cites 29.25 % at a Minnesota pond and 6.6 % at Lower Townline Lake, Michigan, for small fingerlings of 51 and 66 mm, and 1.63 % as the best for fingerlings of 76 mm or more). These are managed, predator-reduced marshes drained in early June, so the survival is an upper reference for a natural lake.
